security_audit.summary: The detected command and filesystem patterns are false positives from Markdown examples, JavaScript template literals, and non-executable resource links. The network examples target public package registries and package metadata services for dependency auditing, with no evidence of hidden exfiltration or prompt injection. Users should still approve outbound scans and mutating remediation commands before execution.

remediation.issue: Outbound dependency lookups may reveal private package names.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit guidance to ask user approval before sending package names to external registries or size services.

remediation.issue: Automated dependency update examples can mutate project files.
remediation.suggestion: State that update scripts require a clean working tree, backups, and user confirmation before force updates or installs.

content.user_title: Audit Dependency Security and License Risk
content.value_statement: Dependency risk is hard to prioritize across vulnerabilities, licenses, updates, and supply chain signals. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured audits and remediation plans.
actual_capabilities: Inventories direct and transitive dependencies from common manifest and lock files.
Checks packages against vulnerability databases and prioritizes issues by severity and exposure.
Reviews dependency licenses for restrictive, incompatible, or unknown terms.
Identifies outdated packages and ranks updates by security value, age, and upgrade effort.
Assesses supply chain signals such as typosquatting, maintainer changes, and suspicious package behavior.
Drafts remediation plans, pull request summaries, and continuous monitoring workflows.
limitations: It depends on available manifest and lock files in the project.
External registry and vulnerability data may be incomplete or delayed.
Suggested upgrades still require tests and staging validation.
License guidance is not legal advice.

use_cases.title: Release Security Review
use_cases.description: Audit dependencies before a release and produce a prioritized vulnerability remediation list.

use_cases.title: Maintenance Upgrade Planning
use_cases.description: Find outdated packages and plan safe updates with compatibility and test impact notes.

use_cases.title: License Risk Assessment
use_cases.description: Identify restrictive, incompatible, or unknown licenses before procurement or open source release.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Dependency Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a broad project review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my project dependencies. Use manifests and lock files in this repository. Report vulnerable, outdated, or risky packages with clear priorities.

prompt_templates.title: License Compliance Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Check license compliance for this project. Use the project license as [LICENSE]. Identify incompatible, restrictive, or unknown licenses and suggest replacements.

prompt_templates.title: Remediation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn findings into a safe upgrade plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a remediation plan for the dependency risks you find. Group fixes by urgency, upgrade effort, and test impact. Ask before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Continuous Monitoring Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a continuous dependency monitoring workflow for this repository. Include vulnerability scans, license checks, update policy, alert routing, and review gates.

output_examples.input: Audit a Node and Python service before release.
output: Executive summary with critical and high vulnerabilities first.
Package-level findings with affected versions, recommended upgrades, and test notes.
Follow-up list for licenses, stale packages, and supply chain checks.
License distribution summary by package group.
List of restrictive, incompatible, and unknown licenses.
Replacement or legal review recommendations for each issue.

output_examples.input: Plan safe dependency upgrades for a legacy app.
output: Prioritized upgrade batches by urgency and expected effort.
Compatibility risks for major version changes.
Validation plan covering tests, staging checks, and rollback notes.

best_practices: Provide all manifest and lock files so the audit can include transitive dependencies.
Approve external scans before sending package names to registries or metadata services.
Run tests and review changelogs before merging dependency upgrades.
anti_patterns: Running force updates without backups, tests, or user approval.
Publishing sensitive vulnerability details outside approved channels.
Treating automated license findings as final legal approval.

faq.question: Which ecosystems can this skill review?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for npm, Python, Ruby, Java, Go, Rust, PHP, and .NET dependency files.

faq.question: Can it automatically fix vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: It can propose and draft remediation steps. File changes or update commands should require user approval.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: Some vulnerability and package metadata checks use public registries or advisory services. Private projects should approve those lookups first.

faq.question: Will it detect transitive dependency risk?
faq.answer: Yes, when lock files or dependency tree data are available. Missing lock files reduce accuracy.

faq.question: Is the license review legally binding?
faq.answer: No. It identifies likely license issues and review needs, but legal counsel should make final decisions.

faq.question: Can it create ongoing monitoring guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline CI checks, alert routing, review gates, and update policies for dependency governance.
